title: Some Voters Ask AI Chatbots About Their Ballots
summary:
Voting in the 2026 midterm elections has started in the United States. Some voters are trying something new. They ask AI chatbots to help them learn about the candidates, NPR reports.

Adam Johnson, 40, lives in Morgantown, West Virginia. One September evening, he spent hours going over his ballot with ChatGPT. He asked it to compare candidates based on what he cares about. He said the chatbot is "kind of a people pleaser."

Other voters use chatbots to learn about small local races and to check claims they see online. Lisa Veldran of Wisconsin used a chatbot called Gemini to compare two candidates for governor. In Pennsylvania, Lakshmi Iyer used a chatbot called Claude to build a website that helps voters.

Experts say to be careful. Rafael Batista of Johns Hopkins University said chatbots may push people toward what they already believe. Chatbots can also give wrong or made-up answers.
why_it_matters: More people are using AI to learn about elections, so it helps to know how these tools work and why their answers should be checked.
